source: Every line traces to the design docs on the bug.games canvas (docs/DECISIONS.md, PUBLISH_DIRECTION, CREATOR_KIT, GUIDE, BOARD_RULES, POSTER_PRINCIPLES, GAMEPAGE, RETURN, HOME_V2, the living-poster CONTRACT, wall.py). Each slot's sources list the doc and its status label. Grounded 20 Oct 2026.

live.title: Needed to go live
live.sub: bug.games' own checks. Fix anything marked ✕ before you publish.

foryou.title: Needed for For You and a full page
foryou.sub: Without these the game still plays from a link, but it isn't shown on For You and its page uses plain placeholders.

optional.title: Optional: makes it shine
optional.sub: Nice to have. Nothing breaks without them.

later.title: When you add more
later.sub: Only needed once the game sells something, has a pass, ships an update or runs an event.

design.title: Store, pass, updates and events · design only
design.sub: For this pass, only the pictures. Nothing goes into the game's code or game.json, nothing is declared and no prices are set. Your chat proposes the items first.

words.title: The page's words
words.sub: Every line on the page that the game writes: the hero, About, controls, details, the seals' names and rules, gallery captions and the game's own voice. No pictures. Numbers, reviews, friends and prices are bug.games'.

slots.label: For You poster
slots.what: The one picture people see on For You, on the game page and in lists.
slots.size: 2:1, at least 1600×800, plus tall (2:3) and square versions, or a moving poster that lays out
must: One image you can name in five words, on the game's own ground, edge to edge
It shows what the game is about: who you are and what you're up against, not only a character's mood
One character in one moment, or one object in one light
A register chosen for the wall: silhouette (one shape holds the world), stage (one lit pocket in the dark) or edition (printed lettering is the art)
Two to four inks, one of them the game's own
The game's own look (medium, line, light, characters), but not the key art itself: no title, buttons, full cast or busy background
Light that visibly comes from a source in the picture
A clear focal path at rest: detail lives where the eye lands
Tall (2:3) and square versions in which the one image still holds; recompose them if a crop loses it
Reads at 90×70
never: Title lettering, numbers, prices, a HUD, a play button, badges, a frame, a border or a vignette (lettering only on an approved Edition poster, on a plate never squeezed below ~200 px)
Anything important in the bottom 26 px (the caption strip) or a busy bottom-left corner (the stamps sit there)
Ember, lilac or sun as a flat block of 24×24 or more, or within 120 px of the caption strip, where Play appears
Changing the game's own colours to pass a check
slots.check: Preview it at 740×370, 260×367, 150×177 and 90×70, and in every wall shape (wall.py). Measure its light band (measure.py light): no light poster beside a light one, no loud beside loud.

Touch is listed whenever inputs includes touch
The action is one or two words in the game's verbs; the note is a few words on when or how
Only controls the game really has
never: A control the build doesn't have
Long notes: on phone the controls show two-up without notes
slots.check: Play with each input using only this list.
slots.example: Night Swim · Space · Swallow · Open wide when a letter is in the beam

sources.line: Controls per input: key, action word, short note; every control for every input; touch whenever inputs has touch
phone shows controls two-up without notes

slots.label: Details and tags
slots.what: 'All details' on About, and the three tags and player count in the hero.
slots.size: genre · players · minutes · inputs · content note · mood · up to 5 tags (the hero shows 3)
slots.file: game.json genre, players, coop, minutes, inputs, contentNote, mood, tags
must: Tags in the game's own words, 2–24 characters each; put the three that say most first
coop only when people play in one session together
A content note when the game has flashing lights or anything a player should know first
A mood word from the platform's list
never: Superlatives, other games' names or prices in tags
'Co-op' for a game where people only see each other's times or ghosts
slots.check: Would the three tags alone sort the game onto the right shelf?
slots.example: Night Swim · Arcade · Quiet · Solo · 1 player · ~15 min

sources.line: All details: genre, players, length, inputs, content note
tags up to five, 2–24 chars, in your words; coop; mood vocabulary; contentNote

slots.label: Seal names and rules
slots.what: Each seal's name (the moment) under it in mono caps, and the one-line rule the plate shows when a player selects it.
slots.size: ≤ 12 moments, in play order; the page shows 8 · one rule line each · a kind each
slots.file: game.json moments · bug/words.json moments [{name, rule, kind: feat | collection | event}]
must: Names in the world's words, short enough for mono caps under a seal
A rule that says exactly what to do, in one line
A kind for each, matching the seal's outline
never: A moment the game can't report
Rarity, progress or dates: those are bug.games'
slots.check: Read the 8 names in a row: do they tell the game's story in order?
slots.example: Night Swim · NIGHT · 'Spell N, I, G, H, T in one swim.' · feat

sources.line: 8 seals with names in mono caps; the plate shows name, rule, progress, rarity

slots.label: Gallery captions
slots.what: The caption under the gallery's main picture. bug.games writes the first half (the slide kind); the game writes the rest.
slots.size: one caption per slide, ≤ about 60 characters after the kind
must: What you see, in the game's words, plain and in its own verbs
never: Text that the picture needs in order to make sense
slots.check: Read the six captions without the pictures: do they walk through the game?
slots.example: Night Swim · 'In the game · the whale, the beam, the letters'

sources.line: Every caption reads <kind> · <what you see, in the game's words>; the game writes the second half, at most about 60 characters

slots.label: Place strings
slots.what: Where a player is, as the game says it. It shows on the Continue card and the phone play bar.
slots.size: each ≤ 30 characters
slots.file: bug/words.json place_strings (the same text the code sends with progress.set)
must: The same text the game sends with progress.set
In the world's terms ('Swim 4', 'Round 2 of 3')
never: Longer than 30 characters: list a longer one as a proposed fix, don't change the code in this pass
slots.check: Does each one tell a returning player where they'll land?

sources.line: place string ≤30, the same text as progress.set

slots.label: The game's voice
slots.what: Small lines bug.games prints in the game's voice: the owned word on store tiles, the line after a buy, the result headline, friend lines, quick chat and the pause line.
slots.size: one verb · stat nouns · own word · bought line · 2–3 result lines · 2 friend lines · ≤ 2 quick-chat lines · 1 pause line
slots.file: bug/words.json verb, stat_nouns, own_word, bought_line, result_lines, friend_lines, quick_chat, pause_line
must: Your world's verbs ('worked', 'stayed', 'hunted', 'Found', 'Filed')
An own word for what owned looks like in the world
Stat nouns the result screen can count ('letters', 'swims')
never: Game-speak ('level', 'enemies'), guilt or exclamation stacks
Streak or scarcity words, 'teardown' or 'Fair Play'
slots.check: Put each line next to the poster: same world, same voice?
slots.example: Night Swim · own word Found · bought line 'Found for you: '

sources.line: one verb, stat nouns; world's verbs; never game-speak, guilt, exclamation stacks
no 'teardown', 'Fair Play', streak or scarcity words

tools.text: The checks name two small Python tools from the bug.games kit: wall.py (puts the poster on the real wall and in every shape) and measure.py (colour zones and light band). Get them at https://github.com/yelnurk123/bug-games-art-pilot/tree/main/kit/tools (Python 3 + Pillow). wall.py saves its two images next to the poster file, so run it on a copy outside bug/. If you can't run them, do the same check by eye and say so.

design.label: Design pass
design.line: This is a design pass: make the pictures and write the page's words only. Don't add anything to the game's code or game.json, don't declare products or a pass, and don't set any prices. Propose the store items, pass rewards, one update and one event first, by name, look and words, and write them to bug/design.json as {"store":{"sub":"…","items":[{"id","name","kind","look"}]},"pass":{"name","unit","desc","rewards":[{"id","name"}]},"update":{"version","title","change"},"event":{"id","name","text","unit"}}. Write every other word on the page to bug/words.json, including drafts of what would go in game.json (title, hook, description, controls, moments, tags).
design.source: Founder, 20 Oct 14:03: "instead of coding the achievements and monetization items into the game this experiment could focus purely on creating the full range of design assets"; "excluding creation of trailer"

wordsNotes.homes: Words that game.json already holds (title, hook, description, genre, minutes, players, coop, inputs, controls, moments, mood, tags, contentNote) live there. The rest go in bug/words.json. In a design pass nothing is written to game.json: draft all of them in bug/words.json under the same names, and they move into game.json after the yes to publish.
wordsNotes.platform: catalogue number, maker and crew handles, loved %, review count and reviews, how many are playing, friends, followers, Shape it requests, 'built from player requests', prices and crumbs, pass step and days left, event count and end time, dates, versions on cards, rarity and progress, NEW and YOURS, 'Nothing you can buy beats other players', More like this and its line, the ticker.
wordsNotes.kicker: The kicker above the title is the latest update's version and title; it comes from the update's words, not a separate line.
wordsNotes.source: Page-contract build.py REQUIRED_DATA (every field the page reads), GAMEPAGE §3, PUBLISH_DIRECTION §3.5, §3.9–3.14, CREATOR_KIT W, the SDK's game.json and manifest.schema.json words.
